interface.title: NoiseQ+ v4.0 — Road Traffic Noise Health Impact Assessment Tool
interface.field: Environmental epidemiology / public health impact assessment (environmental noise)
interface.stage_of_work: Scenario estimation and reporting: turning a population's noise exposure distribution into an estimate of the health burden it causes, then documenting assumptions and uncertainty
interface.what_it_is_for: A guided 6-step wizard that estimates how many cases of heart disease, stroke, heart failure and type 2 diabetes, how many deaths, how many highly annoyed and highly sleep-disturbed people, and how many DALYs a population's road traffic noise causes, with fixed sensitivity tables and a CSV export.

data.note: No files are loaded or uploaded. Every field comes pre-filled with working defaults: population 500,000; band shares 15/25/28/18/9/4/1% for 45–49 … 75+ dB Lden; baseline rates per 100,000 of IHD 285, stroke 215, CVD mortality 480, T2DM 735 and HF 190; reference level 53 dB; Lnight offset 9 dB. I entered Barcelona, Spain, population 1,200,000. Run 1 used threshold mode: 20% above 65 dB, Lnight offset 8 dB, Heart Failure added, IHD baseline set to 300. Run 2 used the detailed bands (11/25/28/18/9/4/5%) with reference levels of 55 dB and then 58 dB. Two CSVs were downloaded under the same file name, noiseq_results_Barcelona__Spain.csv; the second replaced the first.

features.name: Two-mode exposure distribution entry
features.general: Enter how a population is spread across exposure levels, either as shares per band with a live sum-to-100% check, or as one 'percent above a cut-off' figure that the tool expands into a distribution
features.specific: Noise Exposure Data card: choose between 'I have detailed noise data (by 5 dB bands)', with seven % inputs (45–49 … 75+ dB Lden) and a Total that turns red or green and blocks Continue, and 'I only know the percentage above a threshold', with a threshold dropdown (45–70 dB) and a % input approximated by exponential decay
steps: Pick the input mode with one of the two toggle cards
In band mode, type a share for each 5 dB band and watch the Total indicator until it shows 100.0% ✓
In threshold mode, choose the threshold dB and type the % of population above it
Press Continue; it is blocked while the band total is not 100%
Switch modes later: values entered in each mode are kept
serves_tasks: Give the exposure distribution, either in detail or as a single summary figure

features.name: Outcome selector linked to editable baseline rates
features.general: Choose which outcomes to model from cards that show each effect estimate and its source; each chosen outcome adds its own editable background-rate field, which is flagged once it differs from the default
features.specific: Health outcome checkbox cards (RR per 10 dB, age group, citation); ticking Heart Failure adds a Heart Failure baseline field; an edited baseline gets a 'Custom' tag and is listed under 'Custom baseline rates' in Parameters used on Results
steps: Tick or untick outcome cards
Check that the baseline-rate grid shows a field for each ticked disease outcome
Type a local rate per 100,000 per year; a 'Custom' tag appears
View Results: unticked outcomes are dropped from the tables, the chart, the DALYs and the sensitivity tables
serves_tasks: Pick which health outcomes to estimate
Replace the default background rates with local ones

features.name: Reference-level (counterfactual) override
features.general: Show the recommended no-harm reference level, let the user switch on a custom value, and label the results as default or custom
features.specific: 'Reference noise level (counterfactual): 53 dB Lden' badge with a 'Use a different value' checkbox that shows a numeric field; the Results header reads '(WHO guideline)' or '(custom)'
steps: Tick 'Use a different value'
Type a reference dB (e.g. 55 or 58); the heading and badge update
View Results; the header and Parameters used show the custom level, and PAFs and cases change
Untick to go back to 53 dB
serves_tasks: Change the no-harm reference exposure level

features.name: Attributable-burden results report with CSV export
features.general: Show per-outcome attributable counts with confidence intervals, rates and attributable fractions, a bar chart, a disability-adjusted total split into illness and early-death parts, and a list of the parameters used; then export it all as CSV
features.specific: Results step: attributable cases table (cases/deaths per year, 95% CI, rate per 100,000, PAF), people-affected table for annoyance and sleep, 'Attributable cases and deaths by outcome' bar chart, DALY table with YLD/YLL tags and a range, 'Total = YLD + YLL' line, Parameters used, and the buttons Export CSV / Print / PDF / Modify inputs / Sensitivity Analysis
steps: Press View Results
Read the cases table and the bar chart
Scroll to the DALY table and the YLD/YLL total
Check Parameters used (reference level, disability weights, Lnight offset, custom baselines)
Press Export CSV to download the full table and totals
Press Modify inputs to go back to Health Data and rerun
serves_tasks: Read attributable cases and deaths with uncertainty intervals, rates and attributable fractions
Read how many people have the non-disease outcomes (prevalence)
Combine illness and early death into one disability-adjusted total
Export the results table for documentation
Revise the inputs and rerun the estimate

features.name: Assumption-sensitivity comparison tables
features.general: Recompute the main estimate under a fixed set of alternative assumptions (effect-size source, reference level, disability-weight set) and show them side by side, marking the one in use
features.specific: Sensitivity Analysis step: IHD RR source table (4 sources), reference-level table (45/50/53/55 dB × cases and DALYs per outcome) and disability-weight table (WHO 2024 / RIVM 2018 / WHO-JRC 2011), each with a '(used)' tag and an explanatory '?' tooltip
steps: Open Sensitivity Analysis from Results or the step tabs
Compare IHD cases and CIs across RR sources
Compare cases and DALYs across reference levels; the row in use is tagged
Compare annoyance and sleep DALYs across disability-weight sets
Go back to Health Data, change the outcomes or reference level, and reopen: the tables recompute and drop columns for unticked outcomes
serves_tasks: Compare alternative effect-size sources for one outcome
Compare results across reference exposure levels

features.name: Step-tab wizard with progressive unlock and kept state
features.general: A numbered step bar in which later steps unlock as earlier ones are completed, and then allows jumping back and forth without losing any input
features.specific: Tabs 1. Welcome … 6. Methods: they start greyed out, unlock after Continue / View Results, and keep the location, bands, threshold, offset, outcomes, baselines and reference level across jumps
steps: Press Start Assessment; only steps 1–2 are active
Complete a step to unlock the next tab
Jump back to an earlier tab and edit; values are kept
Jump forward to Results, Sensitivity or Methods; they reflect the edits
serves_tasks: Revise the inputs and rerun the estimate
Read attributable cases and deaths with uncertainty intervals, rates and attributable fractions

features.name: Methods transparency panel (formulas and dose-response charts)
features.general: Show the attributable-fraction and exposure-response formulas next to charts of the exposure-response curves, so a reader can see how the estimates were computed
features.specific: Methods step: RR/PAF formula blocks, annoyance and sleep-disturbance polynomial formulas, a dose-response curve chart for annoyance/sleep and an RR-by-Lden chart; the RR chart is fixed at 'reference level 53 dB' and ignores a custom reference level
steps: Open Methods from Sensitivity Analysis or the step tabs
Read the RR/PAF and annoyance/sleep formula blocks
Scroll to the dose-response curve chart and the RR-by-Lden chart
If a custom reference level is set, note that the RR chart still reads 53 dB
serves_tasks: Inspect the formulas and dose-response curves used

screens_never_reached: A printable or PDF view: pressing Print / PDF on Results showed nothing visible in the headless browser (it presumably calls the browser print dialog), so I took no screenshot of it
A sensitivity row for a custom off-grid reference level: with 58 dB the reference-level table stays fixed at 45/50/53/55 dB and no row is tagged '(used)' (screens/024.webp)
A Methods dose-response chart drawn at the user's reference level: it always says 'reference level 53 dB', even with 58 dB set (screens/025.webp)
not_done: Running the sensitivity analyses by choosing a value, as the README wording suggests, cannot be done: the step has no controls. The disability-weight set and the IHD RR source cannot be switched for the main results; the three tables are pre-computed and can only be read and compared.
Print / PDF was pressed but its output could not be seen or checked in the headless browser, so it is not recorded as a task.
No kept screen shows the threshold-mode entry of 65 dB / 20%; the only threshold-mode screen (screens/007.webp) shows the defaults 55 dB / 60%.
The Methods evidence table, limitations and references/citation were not recorded as read; only the formulas and charts are on the kept screens.
I did not try unticking every outcome or entering a population of 0 or a negative value, so the empty and invalid-input states were not explored.
The healthdata.org link points to an external site that is outside the allowed server, so I did not open it.

Defects seen along the way: several tooltips and the DALY methodology text show literal escape codes ('\u2014', '\u20131', '\u00d7') (screens/003.webp, screens/012.webp, screens/022.webp). In the CSV the Location line is not quoted ('Location,Barcelona, Spain'), so 'Spain' falls into an extra column. Both exports use the same file name, so the second replaced the first.
